strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: Diagnostic experiments (Fig. 1) effectively isolate router drift vs. expert drift with clear empirical evidence, distinguishing two failure modes
Comprehensive ablation studies: Table 2 and Figures 3-5 systematically demonstrate individual component contributions with thorough analysis
Technical completeness: Detailed derivations in appendices, pseudocode algorithms (Algorithms 1-2), and layer-wise analysis (Figure 9) showing depth-dependent routing dynamics
Empirical consistency: Improvements are consistent across diverse VQA tasks (ScienceQA to OCR-VQA), not overfitting to specific domains
Practical insights: Formatting-induced forgetting analysis (Figures 6-7) reveals an interesting failure mode with error analysis demonstrating semantic vs. formatting degradation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Spectral decomposition for continual learning is not new (Wang et al. 2023); curvature-aware scaling and expert freezing are established techniques. The combination is incremental rather than introducing fundamental innovations

Unjustified design choices: Multiple critical decisions lack principled justification: energy threshold δ selection (Eq. 4-5), sliding window averaging for singular values (Eq. 7), damped pseudo-inverse constant µ, and AGOP approximation (Eq. 17) only valid for linear experts but applied to complex transformers

Theoretical gaps: First-order Taylor approximation (Eq. 23) may not hold during significant distribution shifts; approximation V⊤⊥x^old ≈ 0 (Eq. 10) is informal with no explicit error bounds; connection between constraints and learned representations unclear

Narrow evaluation: Single benchmark (CoIN with 8 tasks only), single model size (7B), no evaluation on other MCIT benchmarks mentioned in related work; modest improvements (2.8% over HiDe-LLaVA) without statistical significance testing

Missing reproducibility details: No code availability, no sensitivity analysis for hyperparameters (δ, µ, τ_score), unclear computational overhead of covariance maintenance and SVD operations, no error bars or multiple random seeds reported

Presentation issues: Critical justifications (V⊤⊥x^old ≈ 0) relegated to appendix; heavy notation in Section 4 without sufficient intuition; unclear synergistic interactions between the three components; limited discussion of failure modes

Incomplete experimental analysis: Re-routing results only shown for Task 1 (Fig. 4); formatting-induced forgetting seems specific to ScienceQA; no analysis of longer task sequences (>20 tasks) or scaling behavior; hyperparameter selection procedure not described

strengths: Excellent diagnostic analysis clearly decomposing forgetting into router drift and expert drift (Figure 1), with well-designed re-routing experiment that convincingly motivates the proposed approach

Technically sound methodology combining three complementary techniques with solid theoretical grounding: spectral-aware routing (null space projection justified in Appendix A), Riemannian gradient preconditioning (Appendix B), and AGOP-based expert importance

Comprehensive experimental validation with clear ablation studies (Table 2), multiple diagnostic analyses (Figures 3-5), and insightful discovery of formatting-induced forgetting phenomenon (Figures 6-7)
Practical efficiency gains demonstrated: 32.1 min/task training time reduction and 2.3 K MiB/GPU memory savings with adaptive expert activation
Clear presentation with well-structured writing, detailed algorithms (1-2), and extensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Novel insight into how models drift toward new tasks' annotation conventions, revealing a subtle failure mode in continual instruction tuning
weaknesses: Very limited experimental scope: single benchmark (CoIN), single MLLM (LLaVA-v1.5-7B), only 8 tasks, and VQA-only domain; generalization to other architectures and task types is unclear

Modest improvements without statistical rigor: 2.87% absolute gain over best baseline (66.82% vs 63.95%) lacks error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing; number of random seeds not specified, suggesting single-run results
Multiple hyperparameters (δ, μ, ε, λ, τ_score) introduced with no sensitivity analysis or ablation; guidance on setting these is vague ('δ sufficiently close to 1'); design choices appear ad-hoc

Computational complexity not analyzed: SVD cost at each task/layer, whether spectral decomposition overhead negates expert freezing gains, and total training time comparison with baselines not provided

Methodological gaps: sliding window averaging (σ̂_i) lacks clear motivation; Score(i) = Ũ(i) - F̃_pre(i) definition seems ad-hoc without justification; uncentered covariance with LayerNorm justified only by 'empirically small mean'
No convergence analysis or theoretical guarantees; the coupling λ_t = 1/(2η_t) is practical but lacks theoretical justification
Limited exploration of task-specific effectiveness: high performance on ImageNet (90.21%) vs. low on REC (59.87%) not analyzed; unclear which task characteristics favor SAME
Brevity and vagueness in limitations section (one paragraph); does not discuss when SAME fails or is inapplicable; 'ambiguous task boundaries' claim is untested

Technically sound methodology combining spectral decomposition, Riemannian gradient descent, and adaptive expert freezing with rigorous mathematical derivations

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three benchmarks (CoIN, UCIT, TriGap) showing consistent improvements with detailed ablation studies demonstrating complementary contributions of each component
Valuable new TriGap benchmark addressing practical challenges: extended task sequences (10 tasks), domain diversity, and non-uniform data scales

Honest acknowledgment of limitations and clear presentation of both diagnostic analysis and solution design
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—spectral decomposition adapts gradient projection memory ideas, Riemannian preconditioning is established, expert freezing is conceptually straightforward; contribution is primarily in combination rather than fundamentally new methods
Incremental performance improvements without statistical validation: +2.08% on TriGap, +2.87% on CoIN, +1.6% on UCIT; no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests across multiple runs

Key approximations lack rigorous justification: (1) null space assumption relies on vague 'sufficiently close to 1' criterion for energy threshold δ; (2) AGOP proxy (Eq. 17) theoretically valid only for linear experts but LoRA has nonlinear routing interactions; (3) damped pseudo-inverse (Eq. 15) introduces uncharacterized approximation errors

Limited scope and generalization concerns: only LLaVA-7B tested, no evaluation on larger models; FFN-only application with unclear applicability to attention or other adaptation methods; assumes clear task boundaries; restricted to vision-language domain

Methodological inconsistencies: mixed experimental setup with some baselines reproduced and others 'directly adopted from publications'; TriGap benchmark newly constructed making verification difficult for future work; HiDe-LLaVA shows suspicious 31% performance gap between TriGap and CoIN
Sliding window averaging design (Eq. 7) appears ad-hoc with only +3.8% improvement over global averaging but no theoretical justification for why this specific form is superior

Missing statistical rigor and comparisons: no significance tests across runs; no comparison to continual learning methods outside MCIT or knowledge distillation approaches; incomplete analysis of failure modes

strengths: Well-motivated problem analysis: Figure 1 provides clear empirical evidence distinguishing router drift and expert drift as distinct failure modes in MoE-based MCIT
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Extensive ablations (Table 4), sensitivity analyses (Tables 6-9), and multi-benchmark evaluation (CoIN, UCIT, TriGap) with detailed supplementary analyses
Practical contributions: TriGap benchmark addresses important gaps (10-task sequences, domain diversity, non-uniform data scales); efficiency gains of 32.1 min training time reduction per task
Thorough analysis of failure modes: Formatting-induced forgetting (Figs. 6-7), layer-wise routing dynamics (Fig. 10), robustness to task ordering (Tables 7-8) provide useful insights
Clear motivation of three components: Each component addresses a specific identified problem with reasonable intuition and consistent improvements across benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Spectral-aware routing applies standard gradient projection to high-variance subspaces; curvature-aware scaling directly applies established Riemannian optimization; adaptive activation uses simple utilization+importance heuristic. Each component represents incremental combination of existing techniques without significant innovation

Loose mathematical approximations lacking rigor: (1) Null-space projection claim V⊥ᵀXold ≈ 0 relies on informal energy thresholding with no quantitative error bounds or cumulative effect analysis across tasks; (2) Sliding-window scaling (Eq. 7) appears ad-hoc without principled justification vs. alternatives; (3) Low-rank pseudo-inverse damping constant μ=0.9 selected via grid search without analysis of approximation quality

Modest and statistically unclear improvements: TriGap +2.08%, CoIN +2.89%, UCIT +2.93% over baselines—within typical experimental noise (3-5% std dev); no confidence intervals or significance testing; per-task performance varies substantially (10.83%-90.46% on TriGap) with underperformance on some tasks vs. baselines

TriGap benchmark lacks external validation: Newly introduced benchmark with no verification from independent groups; sparse construction details (task selection rationale, quantification of 'diverse formats'); claim of no information leakage unverified; heavy reliance on new benchmark raises overfitting concerns

Incomplete causal analysis of failure modes: Figure 1(d) re-routing experiment conflates multiple sources of representation shift (backbone, non-expert parameters); Table 11 isolates router drift at 0.8-2.1% but relative contribution of router vs. expert drift remains unclear; ablation Table 4 doesn't cleanly separate component importance

Missing theoretical framework: No forgetting bounds or stability guarantees unlike continual learning literature; 'stability' claims lack formal definition; Riemannian metric Cᵗ⁻¹ not justified vs. alternatives (Fisher info, precision matrix); no characterization of failure modes or task/model classes where method is expected to struggle

Presentation and reproducibility gaps: Figure 2 overly complex; five hyperparameters with coupled effects; code availability not mentioned; scalability to larger models (13B, 70B) unexplored; training-time overhead of SVD/pseudo-inverse not quantified; many baseline comparisons from concurrent 2025 work with unclear reproducibility status

Incomplete experimental validation: Simple baselines not compared (freeze all experts except router, freeze router only); sensitivity to window size k and energy threshold δ not fully explored; breakdown of individual component contributions using same three-component setup makes isolation difficult; generalization to non-LLaVA architectures unknown
